records.definition: External resistance relative to capacity, often expressed as %1RM or effort
records.implementation: Use heavier loads for specific maximal-strength practice; a wide range can support hypertrophy if effort and volume are appropriate
Choose a range compatible with goal, exercise, skill and comfort; no magic rep number

records.definition: Repetitions in reserve: estimated additional technically sound reps possible
records.implementation: RIR 3 = stop with about three reps left; useful for autoregulation

records.definition: Perceived exertion scale; in lifting commonly mapped to proximity to failure
records.implementation: RPE 10 ~ maximal effort; RPE 8 ~ roughly 2 reps in reserve; individual estimates are imperfect

records.definition: Heaviest load lifted once with acceptable technique
records.implementation: Direct testing is not required for most users; estimate cautiously from submaximal performance
Longer rests generally help preserve performance in demanding compound work; shorter rests can be used where practical and performance remains adequate
